hills.painterNote: Attempt 2 changes: full-sheet overlapping foundation wash with fresh dip every stroke and ~2x pigment loads, two-coat dark connected oak masses, warmer opaque 2-coat trail — because attempt 1 ran dry (dilute conc, one dip per ~10 strokes) leaving white gaps and ghost values.

judgeNotes.zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash: The sequence opens convincingly with a faint pen underdrawing of the paths and mostly light-before-dark, but the washes and tree masses arrive as rectangular speckle-stamped slabs and the roads turn into straight orange bars that never resolve into the target's winding pale tracks, reading as stamped texture rather than brushwork.
judgeNotes.Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B: The sequence follows a logical progression from sketch to wash, but the washes appear as digital flat blocks rather than brushstrokes.

south-france.painterNote: Attempt 2: ~3x pigment loads at lower water, overlapping full-coverage sweeps, thin separated cypress cores, two-plane sunlit/shaded walls with crisp eaves, grey-olive greens, distant blue hills, and a post-dry dark finishing pen pass — because attempt 1 was washed-out, gappy, and structurally unreadable next to the target's saturated mid-dark values.

judgeNotes.zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash: The sequence reads like a real workflow (pencil block-in, broad light washes, then darks, trees and window detail), but the field and building arrive as flat evenly-toned slabs, a tiny finished white-roof detail shows up by 25%, and the foliage comes in as uniform chip-like dabs dumped in batches rather than varied brushwork.

sargent.painterNote: Attempt 2: deepen all values ~2x into one continuous curved hull mass with a dark bottom waterline band, move the green up and mute it, shrink the rust to small brown flecks and thin the rigging — compare showed a washed-out split hull, missing bottom darks, neon-low green and oversized rust.

judgeNotes.zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash: The opening washes are plausible, but the hull arrives as a flat mask-cut slab with scalloped edges, speckle dots stand in for drawn rigging and hull detail, and the 100% stage never approaches the target's finish, indicating algorithmic fill rather than brush work.
judgeNotes.Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B: The sequence mimics a digital reveal or mask application, showing flat slabs of color and dotted details appearing abruptly rather than organic brushwork.

mittens.painterNote: Attempt 2: push every value range darker (stronger concentrations + layered glazes), redraw tabby as short fur-direction marks with horizontal cheek bars instead of ribbon bands, rebuild hair as small dark near-black interlocking curls instead of gray blocks, strengthen pen lines (higher sepia load) and pupils/eyeliner/brows, and give the man's face an all-over light tan wash with deeper eye/nose/

judgeNotes.zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash: The opening contour sketch is plausibly human, but every wash stage builds form from flat rectangular slabs, stacked horizontal raster bands on the face, and a checkerboard fill in the hair that never resolves into the target's finished rendering.
judgeNotes.Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B: The sequence depicts a digital pattern-fill process with flat color blocks and grid textures, which contradicts the organic brushwork of the watercolor target.

trumbull.painterNote: Attempt 2: lighten stone to a pale warm-tan single wash with shadows as thin glazes only, because attempt 1 was two stops too dark/red and buried windows, roof and sky.

judgeNotes.zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash: A credible painter's sequence — faint pencil block-in, broad sky and mass washes, then roof and window accents, then detail — with only mild flat-slab and scalloped-edge tells in the middle stages.
